page: Google Cloud Platform t2d-standard-8 is a general-purpose virtual machine instance belonging to the Tau T2D machine family. It features 8 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 8 physical cores of an AMD EPYC 7B13 processor, utilizing the x86_64 architecture with a single thread per core configuration. The instance is equipped with 32.0 GB of system memory, providing a balanced allocation of 4.0 GB of RAM per core. It does not include local storage or bundled GPU accelerators, and it offers zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Performance benchmarks indicate strong single-core CPU capabilities, with stress-ng single-core CPU performance placing in the top 25% at 2688.09. Multi-core performance is moderate, with stress-ng multi-core scoring 21511.57 and Geekbench multi-core reaching 7817.0, both falling within the middle 50% tier. Memory bandwidth is also average, registering 95.12 GB/sec for uncached large block reads and 51.75 GB/sec for uncached large block writes. The instance demonstrates steady processing capabilities across standard workloads, achieving a static web serving throughput of 11.61 GB/sec and a Passmark database operations score of 6859.59.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the t2d-standard-8 provides dedicated physical cores without hyperthreading, offering predictable compute performance relative to its resource density. The absence of local NVMe storage and GPU hardware limits its utility for high-speed local database logging or heavy machine learning training. However, its balanced memory-to-vCPU ratio and strong single-thread execution make it appropriate for general-purpose workloads, including web serving, software compilation, text processing, and moderate-scale application hosting.

Lacking hyperthreading, the instance maps 8 physical cores directly to 8 vCPUs, paired with 32.0 GB of system memory at a 1:4 ratio. It contains no local storage or GPU accelerators. This hardware profile delivers predictable compute performance without resource sharing. It is suitable for general-purpose workloads such as web serving, software compilation, and moderate database operations.
